newsitem.title: UK: Smith set for top job after MGAM purge - reports.
newsitem.headline: Smith set for top job after MGAM purge - reports.

text.p: Robert Smith, head of development capital at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, is to take charge of the bank's troubled fund management arm, according to British newspaper reports on Sunday.

A report in the Sunday Times said that Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) chief executive Keith Percy would be one of four top executives to resign this week following a probe into irregular dealings by former fund manager Peter Young.
Smith is poised to replace Percy, the Sunday Times reported. The Sunday Telegraph and the Independent on Sunday also named Smith as the likely new head of MGAM.
But a spokesman for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell dismissed the reports as "premature and speculative."
He said that no action would be taken until a preliminary internal report had been completed and said that this report would be ready only in the next week or so.

The investment banking arm of Deutsche Bank is seeking to establish what went wrong internally and led to the suspension of three MGAM funds last month and Young's dismissal for alleged "gross misconduct."

Trading in the three funds, which totalled around 1.4 billion stg and were held by around 90,000 retail investors, was temporarily suspended early in September but resumed after Deutsche stepped in with a 180 million stg cash injection.

From the beginning Deutsche has made it clear it would take any action deemed necessary to restore confidence in its fund management business and that if lapses in internal controls were found, heads would roll.
The Sunday Times said that Smith had won plaudits since taking charge of the internal inquiry into the Young affair.

The newspaper report said that Glyn Owen, MGAM's chief European investment officer, Mike Wheatley, compliance director for the fund management business and Graham Kane, chief executive of Morgan Grenfell unit-trust managers were also expected to depart along with Percy.
